model for the ζ-function which goes beyond snapshots to also incorporate the
vertical scale.

8.3 The carrier wave and S(t)
The relationship between zero density and the size of the carrier wave can also
be expressed in terms of S(t). Since S(t) is the error term in the zero counting
function, we see that S(t) will be generally increasing in a region where the
zeros are more dense than the local average, and vice-versa. By “generally” we
mean when averaged across a range of several zeros, because of course S(t) is
decreasing wherever it is continuous, and jumps by 1 unit at each critical zero.

section_entries.label: 8 Waves in a unitary polynomial
section_entries.mathematical_role: Exhibits carrier waves, derives a density-wave statistic, relates it to S(t), and studies rigidity and extreme gaps.

unit_result_entry.title: S(t) slope reveals an emergent density wave
unit_result_entry.why_material: Connects increasing or decreasing averaged S(t) to dense or sparse regions and explains carrier waves as collective behavior suppressed at computable heights by rigidity.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: Includes the compatibility caveat with leading-order statistical independence and the reset/anticorrelation explanation.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Prose; figures only illustrate the stated relation.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Density wave as weighted neighbor discrepancy
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Replaces individual gaps with a multiscale density measure, derives a weighted sum of distant-neighbor discrepancies, and matches it to the logarithmic carrier wave.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Matching mean spacing does not determine matrix size
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Exposes a hidden scaling choice in Keating-Snaith and uses carrier-wave amplitude to reject a larger rescaled system with the same local mean gap.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Weighted zero-density discrepancies, averaged S(t) drift, prime-phase sums, and log-correlation are compatible views of the same slow amplitude phenomenon.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The source treats 'arises from' as explanatory language; it does not establish a privileged causal direction or an exact identity among all four models.
related_synthesis_entries.title: One carrier wave, three representations
